problems.source_says: Expressiveness rates the artistic appeal and effectiveness of visual storytelling in each work. These are aesthetic and communicative qualities of a single output. The codebook explicitly includes quality of a single output under usefulness, so this dimension should be coded usefulness; other does not follow that definition. This is a codebook mapping issue, not an error in the transcribed rubric or scores.
problems.quote: Focuses on the artistic appeal, emotional atmosphere, and visual storytelling effect of the work, highlighting esthetic and emotional depth.
problems.locator: PDF p. 12, Table 3, Expressiveness row; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, Construct, usefulness and other definitions (lines 79 and 85).

problems.source_says: Completeness rates coherence, informational adequacy, and the rationality of a design explanation. This assesses the structural quality of a single output and therefore fits usefulness under the codebook. It does not measure elaboration as detail or length, or diversity across people; other is not the appropriate residual category for these quality criteria.
problems.quote: Evaluates the overall coherence, adequacy of information, and rationality of design explanations, including midterm development, extended application, and project presentation.
problems.locator: PDF p. 12, Table 3, Completeness row; creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, Construct, usefulness, elaboration, and other definitions (lines 79, 82, and 85).

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 through S1-O6 are scored on participants' final group projects by six illustration/visual-communication experts, using a 100-point scale; they are not self-reports.

AI was available during production in both arms: embedded throughout the experimental workflow and used sporadically in control sketching or material preparation. All six outcomes correctly answer with_ai, and the comparison is ai_design.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.4.3; p. 11, Table 2; p. 12, Section 3.5.1; codebook Sections 1 and 5.

confirmed.statement: The paper explicitly analyzes 24 projects, supporting unit=output and n_units=24; Table 13 identifies 12 experimental and 12 control projects. The student-level SEM sample is a separate analytical level.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 20, Section 4.6; p. 21, Table 13, W01/Exp through W24/Ctrl.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 is the mean of five distinct dimensions. Its other code describes a mixed design-performance composite, rather than a standalone holistic creativity rating.
S1-O2 correctly uses novelty: the Creativity rubric explicitly evaluates novelty, uniqueness, and innovation of the concept and visual expression.
S1-O3 correctly uses usefulness for alignment with course objectives, application scenarios, and audience needs; S1-O4 correctly uses usefulness for production and craftsmanship quality.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 12, Table 3, Applicability and Technicality rows; codebook Section 6.

summary: Expressiveness and Completeness assess qualities of individual designs and should be coded usefulness under the codebook, so their other construct codes are refuted. Criterion 3 holds because experts scored participants' AI-assisted projects, and all reported outcome numbers match the PDF.
